# Native MCP authorization

Opt-in implementation, disabled until protocol/database tests and live mesh isolation pass. No production schema is installed by startup. See [operator activation and restore handling](../../../docs/authentication.md).

The native client needs an MCP authorization server; Google-backed website cookies alone do not supply client registration or resource-bound access tokens. This package reuses the authenticated browser identity for explicit consent, then issues opaque MCP-only tokens through authorization code + S256 PKCE. PostgreSQL stores only hashes of authorization handles, codes, CSRF values and tokens. Code redemption is atomic; refresh rotation retains replay evidence and revokes its family on reuse.

Public registration accepts bounded exact HTTPS or loopback redirect addresses. Browser authorization is confined to the verified OAuth proxy principal and requires same-origin POST plus a separate secure CSRF cookie. Both the gateway and MCP validate credentials against the private authority; native token checks never trust caller identity headers. Existing registered-user validation remains authoritative. Separate SQL and a non-owner runtime role are required; no startup migration, Google token minting or permissive fallback is allowed.

The implementation follows [MCP authorization](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/authorization) and the [OpenAI client contract](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/auth). Verify publication and actual client login/document reads for each activated release; dated evidence is in [status](../../../docs/status.md).

Run `MCP_OAUTH_BROWSER_TEST=1 go test -race -run TestBrowserConsent ./mcpauth` from `apps/external` after installing the existing `apps/ui` Playwright dependencies and Chromium. This owned loopback fixture exercises actual secure-cookie consent, null/foreign Origin refusal, both decisions and the client callback. Consent pages use `same-origin` referrer policy so native form POSTs retain their Origin; responses otherwise keep `no-referrer`. The form policy includes only self and the previously validated callback origin, since Chromium checks the return redirect too.
